module.description: The import module (`solid-js`, `node:fs`), `lib` for TypeScript's built-in lib.*.d.ts, `global` for a bare global, or a Python package.

name.description: An exported name (`createSignal`). A trailing `*` matches a prefix.

member.description: `Type.method` for a method on an instance (`Session.get`, `Array.find`). A trailing `*` matches a prefix.

args.description: Which arguments the model is about: `0`, `1`, `*` (the default) or `this` for the receiver.

returns.description: What the call yields: `callback` is what the callback at `args` returns; `boolean` a test of it, not it (with `accessor`, on each call of the accessor); `void` is nothing, whatever its callback returns.

source.description: For `calls-back` and `wraps`: the argument whose value (or return) the callback's first parameter receives.

parameters.description: For a standard method's `calls-back`: what each callback parameter takes, in order. An `index` takes no value; an `accumulator` takes the `source` argument and what the callback returned before.

accessor.description: For `calls-back`: the call makes an accessor, and calling it yields the callback's return (or, with `returns: boolean`, a test of it).

option.description: For `calls-back`: the options key that holds the callback (`queryFn`).

lazy.description: For `state-pair`: a function initial value is called, and what it returns seeds the state (`useState(() => …)`).

writes.description: For `consumes`: the receiver keeps the arguments (`push`, `set`). A `consumes` row without it keeps nothing (`concat`).

settles.description: For a promise's member: which outcome each callback takes and what the new promise holds (`PROMISE_CHANNELS`); `reject` makes a promise that only rejects.

proof.description: The proof kind its relations carry, so existing proof names survive.

note.description: One line for the code map and the proof detail.
